correctness.rationale: Modulo the Jacobson radical, the mixed-diagonal triangular matrix is idempotent and the commuting idempotent in any strong clean decomposition is forced to be its complement. A rank-one invariant image or kernel then yields the equation at+b=tc, from which an upper triangular commuting idempotent is constructed; the remaining diagonal entries are units.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Borooah--Diesl--Dorsey explicitly pose the elementwise descent problem, while targeted searches of later strongly-clean and triangular-matrix literature did not locate this n=2 theorem for arbitrary local rings. Full texts of two especially relevant later papers were not inspected, leaving a documented residual risk.

value.rationale: The result resolves the first nontrivial dimension of an explicit open problem without commutativity or bleaching assumptions, and identifies a reusable rank-one invariant-summand mechanism behind triangular descent.
